title: Build from the Back
description: Learn how to move the ball safely from defense into attack!

questions.question: What helps you choose a route out of defense?
options: Look for open space and a teammate with a clear passing lane
Use the sideline even when it is crowded
Pass through the middle even when it is blocked
Choose the longest pass before looking up
questions.explanation: There is no best route every time. Look at the pressure and the receiving player. The open route might be wide, central, or over the press.

questions.question: Why should defenders spread out when starting an attack?
options: To give themselves space to receive a pass
To stand on the same passing line
To leave the central lane empty
To force the goalkeeper to play long
questions.explanation: Spreading creates passing lanes and makes it easier to keep the ball.

questions.question: Who is a useful short option for a goalkeeper with the ball?
options: A teammate showing in a clear passing lane
The nearest defender, even behind a marker
A teammate facing away with pressure on both sides
A teammate pointing while staying hidden
questions.explanation: Being close is not enough. Show where the keeper can reach you and check the pressure around you.

questions.question: The middle is crowded, but the far side is open. What can help?
options: Use a safe pass to switch toward the open side
Force the ball through the closest crowd
Send every teammate toward the ball
Carry the ball toward your own goal
questions.explanation: A switch can open a route forward. It may take more than one pass, including a pass back, to reach that space safely.

questions.question: When a teammate is open on the wing, you should:
options: Pass the ball quickly to them
Hold onto the ball
Dribble into the central pressure
Wait until the defender closes them
questions.explanation: A quick pass to an open wing player moves the attack forward safely.

questions.question: Why do we sometimes take a few small passes instead of one long pass?
options: To keep better control and accuracy
To slow down even when a forward pass is open
Because long passes are never useful
To keep every teammate in the same lane
questions.explanation: Short, accurate passes help keep possession under pressure.

questions.question: What does 'playing out of the back' mean?
options: Building an attack from our defenders and goalie
Clearing the ball as far as possible
Passing between two defenders only
Only dribbling
questions.explanation: It's moving the ball forward with control, starting from defense.

questions.question: If a defender is double-teamed, you should:
options: Offer yourself for a pass in space
Stand on the same line as the defender
Stay in the defender's cover shadow
Move farther from the passing lane
questions.explanation: Moving into space gives your teammate a safe outlet.

questions.question: When building from the back, why is it okay to pass backwards sometimes?
options: It keeps the ball when forward options are blocked
It is only useful when winning late
It is always the wrong direction
It invites pressure if no teammate moves
questions.explanation: A backward pass can reset and open up new spaces to attack.

questions.question: Opponents press high. A teammate is running into open space behind them. What can work?
options: A well-aimed longer pass into that space
A short pass into the closest marked player
A clearance with no look at the runner
Waiting until the runner is surrounded
questions.explanation: A high press can leave space behind it. A longer pass is useful when the target and passing route are realistic, not simply because the press is high.

questions.question: What role does the defensive midfielder play in building from the back?
options: Offers a passing option in front of defense
Runs to the corners
Stays marked behind an opponent
Only defends inside the penalty area
questions.explanation: They link defense and attack by receiving and distributing passes.

questions.question: A forward pass is blocked and a wide teammate is free. What is a good choice?
options: Pass wide through the clear lane
Force the original forward pass
Wait for the wide teammate to be marked
Dribble straight into the blocking player
questions.explanation: Use the available support. If wide options are also blocked, a safe backward pass or a clearance may be better.

questions.question: Why is checking over your shoulder useful when building out?
options: To see where teammates and defenders are
To look only at your own goalkeeper
To turn blindly into pressure
To ignore the defender behind you
questions.explanation: It helps you pick the best passing lane and avoid pressure.

questions.question: What does it mean to 'break a line'?
options: Move the ball past a row of opponents to a teammate or space beyond
Keep passing in front of the same opponents
Send the ball over a touchline
Move every teammate into one straight row
questions.explanation: A pass or dribble can break a line of pressure. Check that the next player can use the ball, not just that the ball gets past someone.

questions.question: The most important thing in building from the back is:
options: Keeping possession and moving safely forward
Scoring on every pass
Only dribbling
Never passing
questions.explanation: Safe, smart passing helps your team control the game and create chances.

questions.question: Why should center-backs split wide when the goalkeeper has the ball?
options: To create bigger passing lanes
To stand closer together in one lane
To block the keeper's passing angle
To stay behind the pressing forward
questions.explanation: Splitting wide stretches the press and gives the keeper safer options.

questions.question: You have room to receive from a center-back. Which body position helps you see forward?
options: Side-on, with a view of the ball and the next space
Facing only the passer until the ball arrives
Facing only the far goal before checking pressure
Standing square and deciding only after the first touch
questions.explanation: An open, side-on position can help you play forward. If a defender is tight behind you, protect the ball and use support instead of forcing a turn.

questions.question: What should the defensive midfielder do during build-up?
options: Show for the ball between or beside opponents
Stay behind a marker
Stand on the goal line
Move beyond the striker too early
questions.explanation: The defensive midfielder can connect defenders to midfield when they find a passing lane.

questions.question: If opponents press one side hard, what can the back line do?
options: Use the keeper or center player to switch sides
Keep forcing passes down the crowded side
All dribble into pressure
Stop creating new passing angles
questions.explanation: Switching through a safe player can escape pressure and find open space.

questions.question: When should you clear instead of build short?
options: When pressure is too close and a mistake would be dangerous
Every time the goalkeeper has it
Never, even inside your own box
Only after the first half
questions.explanation: Playing short is good, but protecting the goal comes first.

questions.question: The keeper and two defenders face two pressing forwards. Why might the keeper remain available for a return pass?
options: To help create a spare passing option and change the angle of attack
To ensure every attack must restart from the goal line
To keep both defenders in the same lane
To avoid ever passing beyond the forwards
questions.explanation: Including the keeper can create a numerical advantage. A return pass is useful only when the keeper has time and a clear next option.

questions.question: A midfielder appears open but has a defender directly behind them. What should the passer consider?
options: Whether the receiver can protect, set, or turn with the ball
Only whether the pass can reach their feet
Only whether they are the nearest teammate
Whether passing forward always counts as progress
questions.explanation: A pass beyond a line is not useful if it traps the receiver. Look at the pressure after reception and the support for their next action.

questions.question: You can carry the ball forward with no opponent close. Why might that be better than an immediate sideways pass?
options: It gains space and may draw an opponent out before the next pass
It means teammates should stop moving
It removes all risk of losing possession
It makes passing unnecessary for the rest of the move
questions.explanation: Carrying can fix a defender, meaning make them choose whether to leave their position and engage. Keep scanning and release before the space closes.

questions.question: A full-back moves into midfield during build-up. What is the useful idea behind this movement?
options: Create another central passing option while teammates maintain width and cover
Put every defender into midfield together
Make the player stop defending for the rest of the game
Keep the same team spacing regardless of the movement
questions.explanation: An inverted full-back moves inward in possession. It can help connect passes and protect central space, but teammates must adjust around that movement.

questions.question: Your short build-up has drawn several opponents forward, but their back line leaves space behind. What should you consider?
options: A longer pass to a reachable target if that route is now open
Continuing short passes regardless of the pressure
Waiting until all opponents retreat before advancing
Using a long pass even if nobody can reach it
questions.explanation: Building from the back is not a rule to pass short forever. Drawing a press can create a useful longer route over or through it.
